# Built-in tools

The tool surface the model sees, generated from the registry (advertisement order). Behaviour and limits are explained in [Tools](../guide/tools.md).

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `read` | Read a text file as 1-based numbered lines (N\| text). Returns up to 400 lines or 24 KiB by default, with truncation noted; an explicit limit caps at 2000 lines. A negative offset reads the last N lines. Lines over 500 characters are cut. |
| `bash` | Run a shell command in bash; returns merged stdout+stderr and the exit code. Output keeps the start and end when over 10 KiB. Nonzero exits are errors that still include the output; a timeout or abort reports any partial output. A command that may outlive the timeout takes background: true: it keeps running as a job and the result names it; wait_for: &lt;id> waits for that job and returns its output; stop: &lt;id> kills it. wait_job: &lt;name> waits for a detached job the command registered in the run's job log ($GG_JOB_LOG), with a wait budget of its own. A `gg -p` started here is a nested run: it keeps this run's tools, hooks, model and limits. |
| `edit` | Apply exact-match edits: each old_text must appear exactly once unless the edit sets replace_all: true, and any miss or ambiguity writes nothing. |
| `write` | Create or overwrite a file. Refuses paths outside the working directory unless force is true; reports bytes written. |
| `grep` | Search file contents by regex, or literal text with fixed_strings. Respects .gitignore and skips .git, target, node_modules and binaries. Results are grouped by file; supports glob, case_insensitive, context lines and files_only; caps at max_results (default 50) and 16 KiB of output. |
| `find` | Find files and directories by glob (e.g. "*.rs", "**/*.md"). Respects .gitignore and skips .git, target and node_modules by default (include_ignored: true to include them). Sorted and capped at max_results (default 50). |
| `ls` | List one directory level: directories (name/) then files with byte size, alphabetical. Not recursive; use find for deeper paths. Hidden entries included; unreadable entries are noted, not fatal. |
| `outline` | Return a compact structural outline of a file: symbol or heading signatures with 1-based line ranges, so you can jump straight to read(offset, limit). Supports Rust, Python, JS/TS, Go, C/C++/Java/C#, shell, Markdown and TOML. |

## `read`

Read a text file as 1-based numbered lines (N| text). Returns up to 400 lines or 24 KiB by default, with truncation noted; an explicit limit caps at 2000 lines. A negative offset reads the last N lines. Lines over 500 characters are cut.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum lines to return (default 400, max 2000) |
| `offset` | integer | no | 1-based line to start at; negative reads the last N lines |
| `path` | string | yes | File path relative to the working directory, absolute, or starting with ~ |

## `bash`

Run a shell command in bash; returns merged stdout+stderr and the exit code. Output keeps the start and end when over 10 KiB. Nonzero exits are errors that still include the output; a timeout or abort reports any partial output. A command that may outlive the timeout takes background: true: it keeps running as a job and the result names it; wait_for: <id> waits for that job and returns its output; stop: <id> kills it. wait_job: <name> waits for a detached job the command registered in the run's job log ($GG_JOB_LOG), with a wait budget of its own. A `gg -p` started here is a nested run: it keeps this run's tools, hooks, model and limits.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `background` | boolean | no | For a command that may still be running at the deadline: keep it running as a job and name it in the result instead of killing it. Collect the job later with wait_for |
| `command` | string | no | Shell command to run (required unless wait_for, wait_job or stop is set) |
| `stop` | integer | no | Kill background job &lt;id>, whole process group included. Takes no command |
| `timeout_secs` | integer | no | Kill the command after this many seconds; the most this session allows is 300, and a larger value is refused. A command always keeps that ceiling, and wait_for waits it by default. A wait (wait_for or wait_job) may pass a budget past the ceiling: wait_job defaults to 600 s, both clamp to 3600 s |
| `wait_for` | integer | no | Wait for background job &lt;id> and return its output and exit code. A job still running when the budget passes is reported with its output so far. Takes no command |
| `wait_job` | string | no | Wait for the detached job a command registered under this name in the run's job log ($GG_JOB_LOG): a start record (name, pid, directory) when it started, a done record (name, exit, note) when it ended. Waits until the done record lands or the pid is gone; a job still running when the budget passes is reported with its progress so far. Takes no command |

## `edit`

Apply exact-match edits: each old_text must appear exactly once unless the edit sets replace_all: true, and any miss or ambiguity writes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `edits` | array of object | yes | Edits applied in order, atomically |
| `path` | string | yes | File to edit, relative to the cwd, absolute, or starting with ~ |

## `write`

Create or overwrite a file. Refuses paths outside the working directory unless force is true; reports bytes written.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | string | yes | Full file content |
| `force` | boolean | no | Allow writing outside the working directory |
| `path` | string | yes | File to create or overwrite, relative to the cwd, absolute, or starting with ~ |

## `grep`

Search file contents by regex, or literal text with fixed_strings. Respects .gitignore and skips .git, target, node_modules and binaries. Results are grouped by file; supports glob, case_insensitive, context lines and files_only; caps at max_results (default 50) and 16 KiB of output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `case_insensitive` | boolean | no | Case-insensitive matching (default: false) |
| `context` | integer | no | Context lines before and after each match (max 10) |
| `files_only` | boolean | no | Emit each matching file with its match count instead of lines (default: false) |
| `fixed_strings` | boolean | no | Treat pattern as literal text, not regex (default: false) |
| `glob` | string | no | Glob filter on file names or paths, e.g. "*.rs" |
| `max_results` | integer | no | Maximum matching lines to return (default 50) |
| `path` | string | no | File or directory to search, relative to the cwd, absolute, or starting with ~ (default ".") |
| `pattern` | string | yes | Regex, or literal text when fixed_strings is true |

## `find`

Find files and directories by glob (e.g. "*.rs", "**/*.md"). Respects .gitignore and skips .git, target and node_modules by default (include_ignored: true to include them). Sorted and capped at max_results (default 50).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_ignored` | boolean | no | Include .gitignore'd, target/ and node_modules/ entries (default: false) |
| `max_results` | integer | no | Maximum paths to return (default 50) |
| `path` | string | no | Directory to search from, relative to the cwd, absolute, or starting with ~ (default: the working directory) |
| `pattern` | string | yes | Glob matched against entry names, or relative paths when it contains '/' |

## `ls`

List one directory level: directories (name/) then files with byte size, alphabetical. Not recursive; use find for deeper paths. Hidden entries included; unreadable entries are noted, not fatal.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | no | Directory to list, relative to the cwd, absolute, or starting with ~ (default: the working directory) |

## `outline`

Return a compact structural outline of a file: symbol or heading signatures with 1-based line ranges, so you can jump straight to read(offset, limit). Supports Rust, Python, JS/TS, Go, C/C++/Java/C#, shell, Markdown and TOML.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_entries` | integer | no | Maximum entries to return (default 200, max 500) |
| `path` | string | yes | File path relative to the working directory, absolute, or starting with ~ |
